description: Today `bin/chief run` is the only entry point and it is built for a human terminal — a colored schedule and a summary meant to be read, not parsed. A host app embedding chief (a Cuneiform Riju agent, or chief-cloud) that wants to START a run and READ its outcome must either scrape the interactive stdout or invoke `engine/driver.sh` against an undocumented contract. This tasklist adds a stable, non-interactive invocation path over the SAME engine (no loop rewrite): configuration in via the existing env/flags, a parseable run-id + machine-readable outcome out, and a documented, deterministic exit-code contract. It is the foundation the status stream (81) and run-in-container (84) build on. Scope: `bin/chief` (a headless/JSON mode on `cmd_run`), `engine/driver.sh` (emit the run-id line + a final machine summary at points it already reaches), and `docs/`. The run-id is the `<repo>-<cksum>-<epoch>-<pid>` id driver.sh already mints (~L157) and exports as `CHIEF_RUN_ID`.

userStories.title: A non-interactive run entry point that prints the run-id
userStories.description: Add a headless mode to `chief run` (a `--headless` flag, and/or suppress TTY-only output when stdout is not a terminal — pick one and document it) so a parent process can drive a run with no interactive behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: `chief run --headless [names…]` runs the scheduler with NO TTY-dependent behavior: no ANSI color, no interactive prompt, line-oriented parseable output; it accepts all config already supported (`-p N`, `--no-merge`, `--provider`, `--model`, and the `CHIEF_PROVIDER`/`CHIEF_MODEL`/`CHIEF_PROJECT` env) with no new interactive step

Before the loop begins, the run prints its `CHIEF_RUN_ID` (the id minted in `engine/driver.sh` ~L157) to stdout on a stable, greppable line (e.g. `chief: run-id=<id>`), so a host can correlate the run with `$CHIEF_RUNS/<pid>.run` and the state dir
Human/interactive `chief run` output is unchanged when `--headless` is not in effect and stdout is a TTY (the colored schedule + summary still print)

userStories.title: A deterministic exit-code + machine-readable outcome contract
userStories.description: A host must be able to tell what happened from the exit code and a parseable summary, without scraping the human summary block.
acceptanceCriteria: The headless run exits with documented, deterministic codes that distinguish at least: all requested tasklists merged (0); nothing runnable / no-work (a distinct non-zero); ≥1 tasklist ended VERIFY-FAILED; ≥1 REBASE/MERGE-CONFLICT; a bad-repo / config error. The exact table is written in docs and asserted by a test

A machine-readable end-of-run summary is emitted (a final JSON object, or a `--json` summary) naming each requested tasklist and its terminal state (merged / verify-failed / blocked / conflict) plus the run-id — enough to render an outcome with no scraping
The exit-code mapping is derived from the terminal states the driver already computes for the human summary — this story surfaces them, it does not add a second state machine

userStories.title: Document the embedding contract and test it hermetically
userStories.description: The whole point is a stable contract a host codes against; write it down and pin it with a test in the existing hermetic suite.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/` gains an "Embedding chief / headless invocation" section: the entry point, env/flags in, the run-id-out line, the exit-code table, and the summary shape

A hermetic test (scripted fake `claude` on PATH, temp `CHIEF_*` prefixes, per `test/{smoke,ratelimit,…}.sh`) asserts: the run-id line is emitted and parseable; the exit code matches the outcome for a merged run and for a verify-failed run; the JSON summary is valid JSON with the documented fields. It joins the behavioral subset the verify hook + CI run
